summary: Daisetsu Teitaro Suzuki was a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Waseda University, the University of Tokyo, and under Kōsen Imakita, Soyen Shaku, and Paul Carus. He held professorships at Otani, Columbia, and Gakushuin universities.

Daishun Ueyama worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology, having studied under Akira Fujieda. He spent his career at Ryukoku University as an associate professor, professor, and university president.

Daisy Cheung is a scholar of Indology and Tibetology who earned degrees at the University of Hong Kong and completed her Ph.D. at the University of Hamburg. Her posts include research roles at the University of Hong Kong and the Austrian Academy of Sciences.
Daito Shimaji was an Indologist and scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied at Ryukoku and Otani universities. He taught at Komazawa, Rissho, Toyo, and Tokyo universities.

Dale S. Wright is a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and religious studies who studied under Alan Anderson, Wang Pachow, and Robert P. Scharlemann. He served as a professor of religious and Asian studies at Occidental College.

Dalpat Rajpurohit specializes in Indology, having earned degrees from Jai Narain Vyas University, Jawaharlal Nehru University, and Presidency University. He taught Hindi and Urdu at Columbia University and became an assistant professor at the University of Texas at Austin.

Dalsukh Malvania was a scholar of Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies. He held posts at Banaras Hindu University, Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda, the University of Toronto, and served as director of the L.D. Institute of Indology.
Damaru Chandra Bhatta is an Indologist and philosopher who earned a Ph.D. from Tribhuvan University. In 1994, he was an associate professor at Tri-Chandra Multiple Campus.
Damchö Gyatso studied under Penor Rinpoche, Dodrupchen Rinpoche, and Dzongsar Jamyang Khyentse Rinpoche.
Damdin Badaraev was a scholar of Tibetology and linguistics who studied under Bidia Dandaron and George de Roerich.

Damien Keown is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and philosophy who earned degrees from Lancaster University and the University of Oxford. He served as professor of Buddhist ethics at Goldsmiths, University of London.

Damodar Dharmananda Kosambi was an Indologist and historian who studied at Harvard University under George David Birkhoff. He held professorships at Banaras Hindu University, Fergusson College, and the Tata Institute of Fundamental Research.

Dan Arnold is a scholar of philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology who studied at Carleton College, Columbia University, Iliff School of Theology, and the University of Chicago. He held faculty posts at McGill University and the University of Chicago.
Dan Li is a scholar of linguistics and Buddhist studies who studied under Sherab Gyatso. He holds an associate professorship at Soka University.

Dan Lusthaus is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned his Ph.D. at Temple University. He held academic posts at Grinnell College, Bates College, the University of Georgia, Florida State University, and Harvard University.

Dan Martin is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who studied at Ohio State University, Kent State University, and Indiana University Bloomington. He has held positions at Hebrew University of Jerusalem, Carnegie Mellon University, and Swarthmore College.

Dan Smyer Yü works in religious studies and Tibetology, earning a Ph.D. from the University of California, Davis. He served as a research group leader at the Max Planck Institute for the Study of Religious and Ethnic Diversity.

Dan Zahavi is a philosopher who studied at KU Leuven under Rudolf Bernet and at the University of Copenhagen. He has served as a professor of philosophy at the University of Copenhagen and held a post at the University of Oxford.
Daniel Aaron Getz is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology who earned his Ph.D. at Yale University under Stanley Weinstein. He has served as an associate professor at Bradley University.
Daniel Amadé Scheidegger is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies who earned a doctoral degree at the University of Bristol under Paul Williams.
